cells.tense: You are here, mind weighing two things before it commits.
cells.act: let the structure act instead of announcing it
cells.ask: When the next call comes and the two options sit level, claim one and move on it that same day — no walkthrough, no summary after. The choice does the explaining.
cells.core:
You've got a mind that can hold two sides at once, and right now that skill is serving you. You weigh the call before you make it, and the call lands better for the weighing. The mix you're adjusting is working — not frozen, not lurching, tuned as the day asks.

What comes next is putting that judgment somewhere it can stand without you narrating it. Take the next thing that's yours to settle — something small — settle it, carry it through, and let it speak for itself. No speech is required about why it's right. A decision that arrives cleanly tells people more than the reasons do. Then what's in your hands is the thing itself, not the version kept in your head.
cells.sheetLine: A settled call outlasts the reasons you'd rehearse.
cells.verb: holding two truths level before you say which one
cells.place: where the mix is being adjusted — a little added, a little taken, as the moment asks

cells.tense: You are leaning into a moment you are sure you will have to defend.
cells.act: go on toward it without needing a sign
cells.ask: Keep what you already chose moving for the next seven days — no hunting for confirmation, no proof you were right, no fence built before you start.
cells.core:
The weighing has turned into bracing. Two truths are still in your hands, but the hands have tightened, and you're rehearsing a moment that hasn't arrived — the argument, the defense, the version where someone asks how you could be sure. A future is getting written before it gets here, and the present is being skipped to reach it.

Go on toward what you already settled. No sign is owed before the next step, and the defense doesn't need to be ready before the question is asked. The proof shows up in the doing, not before it. Give it a week of ordinary motion and hear what the week says back. More thinking won't quiet the worry. It gets smaller when the thing is simply being done.
cells.sheetLine: Stop rehearsing the defense. Move the thing you already chose.

cells.tense: You are standing at a threshold that is already behind you.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Spend an hour inside something you finished — the meal you cooked, the page you wrote — and improve nothing. Nothing gets polished.
cells.core:
The mind that usually weighs is out of the room. A call got made, or a thing got completed, and you moved past it without letting it arrive. You show up, you do the work, and none of it lands as finished — a next thing is already pulling at the sleeve. What you know is still there; nothing has asked it to say so.

Go be inside something you already made. Use it, look at it, take an hour with it, and touch nothing while you're in there. Don't fix, don't polish, don't start the next version. Finished things give something back when you stop touching them, and that's the only way to find out what yours have been holding. That threshold is behind you — turn around and stand in it a minute.
cells.sheetLine: Something you finished is still waiting to be lived in.

cells.tense: You are in a room already writing, and you would call yourself only a passer-through.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: When an offer comes toward you, accept it rather than deflecting — and when you give, allow it to come back. One exchange, both directions, no ledger.
cells.core:
A weighing is going on in you that you haven't put your name on. You read a room, you sense what's fair, you know when to step back — and if someone said so, you'd shrug it off as normal. Your judgment is doing the work, and your account of it leaves out that it's yours.

Let something move in both directions with another person. Accept the offer you'd normally deflect, and when the favor comes back, don't chase it off. No accounts need keeping, and no explanation is owed about the ones you haven't kept. The other person is already treating it as an exchange — you can too. That's the whole move: it was yours the whole time, and naming it doesn't require a speech.
cells.sheetLine: You're already in the exchange. You'd just rather not say so.

attempts.check: The draft's weakest claim is reading 'Reflection' as a capacity to hold two truths before deciding, when the person may simply experience it as ordinary carefulness — the reader could reasonably say that's just how anyone thinks before speaking. The asks survive being wrong because each is a small outward act (put it down in words; keep going a week; sit in something finished; let an exchange run both ways) that teaches something regardless of the diagnosis. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any phrasing that implies the mind's pause is a gift rather than a habit — cut that framing from every cell.
